question.text: The adjoining diagram shows three soap bubbles A, B and C prepared by blowing the capillary tube fitted with stop cocks, S1,S2 and S3. The bubble B is the largest and the bubble C is the smallest. With stop cock S closed, what will happen when we open the stop cocks S1,S2 and S3 simultaneously?

options.text: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> will start collapsing with volumes of  <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> increasing

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> both will start collapsing with the volume of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> increasing

Volumes of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> will become equal at equilibrium

solution.text:
Excess pressure inside soap bubble is inversely proportional to the radius of bubble i.e. ΔP∝1r

This means that bubbles A and C posses greater pressure inside it than B. So the air will move from A and C towards B.
